newsitem.title: USA: Ford signs key magnesium agreement.
newsitem.headline: Ford signs key magnesium agreement.

text.p: Ford Motor Co said Wednesday it became a partner in a magnesium production plant in Australia, joining the Australian Magnesium Corp and the Australian government to build a pilot plant in Gladstone, Queensland.

It said the agreement guarantees the auto company a long-term, stable supply of high-grade, low-cost magnesium metal. Australian Magnesium is a joint venture between Queensland Metals Corp NL and Normandy Mining Ltd.
Queensland Metals and the Australian government launched a joint project 10 years ago to develop a low-cost process for converting magnesite to magnesium.
Ford said it will invest $30 million in a pilot study of the technology.

"This multi-billion contract will provide Ford with a steady stream of high-quality, low-cost magnesium well into the 21st century," Carlos Mazzorin, vice president Purchasing-Ford Automotive Operations, said in a statement.
Ford also has signed a multi-year contract with Australian Magnesium Corp to buy about half the magnesium produced at the pilot plant -- in excess of several thousand tons annually.
Worldwide, Ford said it uses about 14,000 tons of magnesium components every year, or 2.5 pounds of magnesium components per vehicle.
